summary: Iteration 13: Unity Port catch-up accrual (maybe_accrue) and the new admin Global Momentum Tree page. Local DB sim: 12/12 pytest passed. Atlas read-only checks: 21/21 passed (the 2 'FAIL' lines in the raw output came from a case-sensitive assertion in my script on checksum addresses; the data was correct). UI: admin /admin/gm-tree and member /ports/unity work. At test time (18:39-18:44Z) it was BEFORE the first due payout at 2026-11-05T19:30Z, so I could NOT confirm the 0.5004/0.5004/1.0 port_daily_earnings records on Atlas. I only confirmed that nothing was paid early.

minor.issue: Slow on Atlas: 2.3-3.3s per call. It loads every GM matrix node on each request to build the day list, and the day list is always the whole tree, not filtered when ?root= is set. Fine at 2 members, but cost grows linearly. Consider aggregating by IST day in Mongo and/or paginating.

The throttle timestamp is set before accrue runs. If accrue fails (e.g. a price fetch error), the next retry is 15 min later; the error is logged via _done. It is also per-process: the guard is in memory only, so N workers run up to N accrues per 15 min. This is safe because of the optimistic lock on accrued_days, which I verified with concurrent gather.

ui_bugs.issue: GmTree passes isSelf to BoardTree, so in the admin view the company-root spot is labelled 'YOU', and so is any focused wallet. The admin is not that wallet, so this is misleading. Pass isSelf={false} or show a 'ROOT'/short-address label.

No loading indicator. During the ~3s fetch, KCards show 0/0/'—' and the panels say 'The Global Momentum tree is empty.' / 'No one has joined...'. This looks like real empty data. For an unknown wallet, react-query's default retries (3x on 404) mean gm-error only appears after several seconds, and the KCards drop to 0 meanwhile. Use isLoading + placeholderData/keepPreviousData, and set retry:false for 404.
useState(days[0]?.date) is set on the first render, when days is still []. Because of that, the newest day is never auto-expanded; the user must click it.

issues: Days are grouped by IST date ('Nov 6, 2026'), but join timestamps use the browser's local time ('Nov 05, 06:31 PM' on a UTC browser). Show the time in IST to match the grouping.
'next payout' uses browser-local time without a timezone label. Consider appending IST, or showing '01:00 IST'.

critical_code_review_comments: maybe_accrue runs a full accrue over every active purchase every 15 min for any member hit. Fine at the current scale, and it is idempotent via the optimistic lock on accrued_days. accrue still awaits credit() after claiming the days, so a crash between the claim and credit() would lose that payout (not retried).
gm_tree day list ignores ?root and scans all GM nodes on every call
